Mass Effect fans are urging Japanese studio Pocketpair, known for Palworld, to buy the rights to the sci-fi series from Electronic Arts and save its future. According to Pocketpair's Head of Communications and Publishing, Jon “Bucky” Buckley, he has received almost 30 direct messages and emails with similar requests in the last 24 hours alone.

Buckley shared this on social media, noting that such reactions regularly occur after game studios close or projects are canceled. Fans approach Pocketpair with suggestions like “You should buy this franchise!” Over time, according to the company representative, such requests can turn into complaints: players start asking why the studio never acquired the rights, as they supposedly have enough money.

Buckley emphasized that buying game franchises is much more complex than it seems from the outside. Intellectual property owners are often not interested in selling, and the asking price can be unreasonably high.

However, Buckley himself has another candidate for a potential acquisition. In response to the wave of suggestions to buy Mass Effect, he humorously remarked that the rights to Jade Empire would interest him much more. This role-playing game was also created by BioWare but never received a sequel.

The legendary studio was responsible for many beloved RPGs, including the Mass Effect series, for which a new installment was deep in development. In the aftermath, fans have been scurrying for ways to salvage the project, including courting Palworld developer Pocketpair.

No, seriously - and apparently this isn't the first time that's happened, either. "Soon after a game is canceled or a studio shuts down, we get a lot of comments and emails from fans saying 'You should buy this IP!'" John 'Bucky' Buckley, head of communications and publishing at Pocketpair, posted on Twitter .

"Then, as months go by, those comments turn into 'Why didn't you buy it? You have the money!'" he adds, before explaining the reality that buying and selling IP is complicated, and often the asking price is obscene compared to the potential value. He then points out that, yes, people have been bugging him about Mass Effect 5.

Soon after a game is cancelled or a studio shuts down, we get a lot of comments and emails from fans saying "You should buy this IP!" Then, as months go by, those comments turn into "Why didn't you buy it? You have the money!" The reality is, in my experience at least, the IP holders often have absolutely no interest in selling and when they do, the asking price is absurd... It's becoming a more common topic these days, because so many games are being cancelled or shut down, so I just wanted to share my personal experience. Plenty of companies do try to buy or at least license game IPs to keep them alive. But...if the IP holder doesn't want to play ball...then there isn't much anyone can really do :/ October 22, 2026

"I got close to 30 DMs/emails from fans about buying Mass Effect in the last day," he says in response to someone asking. He then jokes that Jade Empire would make him more keen.

Pocketpair saving the new Mass Effect would be a plot twist and a half on this whole debacle, but I suspect it's wishful thinking at best. Despite the fact the studio seems to be doing well, who knows if EA would even be open to conversations around selling the sci-fi property, and if it was, whether the amount wanted would make any kind of sense.

EA killing BioWare could lead to Mass Effect and Dragon Age rights being sold, ex-studio lead says Former Mass Effect and Star Wars: KOTOR boss calls BioWare closure "sad" Mass Effect 5 was "special", dev says, and BioWare's response to Baldur's Gate 3 and Cyberpunk 2077 I'm not sure it's a great fit to fly BioWare 's flag, either. Palworld and the spin-offs that have been revealed are very different to the expansive role-playing games that make up the home of Dragon Age's repertoire. You don't want just anyone making the next Mass Effect - you want a studio that'll honor the existing work and legacy.

Ultimately, those who could've given us a sequel worthy of the first trilogy have just been let go. Mourn what could've been, and let the bargaining stage pass. And then boot up the first Mass Effect yet again.

Earlier this week, Palworld announced "Side by Side," which may sound like a subtitle for a sequel or spinoff, but it's actually just the name of the next update for the game, set to release in Winter 2026. It even came with mysterious key art that clearly had some people thinking it was something huge, prompting Pocketpair head of publishing and communications John "Bucky" Buckley to set the record straight.

Over on Twitter, Bucky notes, "Palworld Side by Side is v1.1 by the way." He continues, "I thought that was pretty clear, but it seems quite a few people thought it was a new game announcement." So if you were expecting "Palworld 2 with terrain modification and underwater biomes" like one (joking) response, I'm afraid that's not happening.

Palworld Side by Side is v1.1 by the way! I thought that was pretty clear but, it seems quite a few people thought it was a new game announcement. Anyway…it’s an update. For Palworld. v1.1 😇 October 22, 2026

So what does it involve? While we don't yet know, speaking to MP1st recently, Bucky explains that "we’re not quite ready to start teasing it just yet." However, he did reveal one note about what to expect from Palworld Side by Side's 1.1 update, saying, "1.1 isn’t a massive update," but that "we do think players will be pretty happy with it."

One thing you can rule out is Palworld Side by Side adding "100 new Pals," as Bucky said in the same interview that Pocketpair developers "try to add Pals in a meaningful way. " We got 72 new pals in the massive 1.0 patch a few months back , so I don't expect we'll see many new additions – if any – this time around.

items.title: Palworld Patch 1.1 Is Not a “Massive Update,” Pocketpair Comments on Expansions
items.summary: Pocketpair confirms to MP1st that Palworld's 1.1 update won't be a "massive" patch, as the devs also comment on DLC and expansions.
items.content:
With the launch of Palworld to version 1.0 , the game has seen a tremendous uptick in player counts.

Version 1.0 was released in July of this year, and given we’re in the last few months of 2026, it’s understandable that players are looking forward to the next major update.

It seems the next version jump won’t be it, as we asked the developers about Palworld update 1.1, and the comment we received might not be what the player base wants to hear right now.

Speaking to MP1st in an exclusive interview, Pocketpair’s John “Bucky” Buckley, the studio’s Head of Publishing and Communications, answered our questions on not just update 1.1, but even about expansions/DLC.

MP1st : When will players hear more about Update 1.1, and can you reveal what highly requested feature it will introduce?

Bucky answered, “An answer that no one wants, but everyone expects… you’ll have to wait just a little longer!”

Adding more to it, Buckley said, “While 1.1 isn’t a massive update, we do think players will be pretty happy with it! That said, we’re not quite ready to start teasing it just yet!”

Let’s hope that version 1.1 will at least have something new for players… even if it’s not big in terms of scale.

Just for reference, the 1.0 patch for Palworld brought the following:

While I doubt anyone expects the version 1.1 patch to be anywhere close to this, the player base might still expect something tangible, given it’s been months since a proper version-jump patch was released.

In the same chat, we asked Buckley about the possibility of a Palworld expansion or DLC.

MP1st : Will future Palworld content be free or paid? Not just game updates, but actual content?

Buckley answered, “To be honest, we don’t really think about future content in terms of whether we should monetize it or not.”

Continuing with the topic, Buckley added, “So far, we’ve been happy to continue supporting Palworld through free updates, and we haven’t felt the need to approach things differently. Of course, we wouldn’t completely rule out the possibility of something larger, like an expansion, in the distant future, but we have no specific plans to announce and it’s not something we’re actively working towards right now.”

Alongside the occasional small patch, Palworld has just had its next big update announced for Winter 2026.

Officially dubbed the “Side by Side update,” the teaser image for it shows a few of the human Palworld Tower Bosses posing with weapons in their hands. Combine these two facts, and it seems to imply that this update will add the defeated bosses as potential companions for you to recruit as part of your adventure – a highly requested feature.

Source: Pocketpair Alongside this news come the results of the popularity poll that was released last month, finding out who the Palworld community likes the most. With two polls conducted, one for Pals and one for humans, the top picks for each have been revealed.

In the human category, the results are, frankly, predictable. Zoe came out on top yet again. As she is the first Tower Boss in the game, and currently the only one with a storyline following her defeat, it makes sense that she would be the character players have the deepest connection with.

Source: Pocketpair However, there may be more at play, as it’s worth pointing out that all five female characters took the top five spots, with the player character (who can be either gender) taking sixth, and everyone from seventh down being men. Do with that information what you will.

The Pal category was also unsurprising, as of all the new Pals added since the game first launched into early access, none have captured the community’s imagination like Sekhmet, the poll’s winner. Her cutesy catgirl aesthetic is an immediate draw, and combine that with the cute way she dances while idling around your base, and you have a sure-fire winner. Solenne took second place, while one of the game’s mascots, Chillet, took third.

items.title: Palworld’s Next Big Update “Side by Side” Launches This Winter
items.summary: Pocketpair will share more "soon", but the update's first teaser image implies two more Tower bosses will become recruitable.
items.content:
Following a very successful early access exit last July, Pocketpair has announced that the first major post-launch update for Palworld , Side by Side, will go live this Winter. The timing implies a reveal at The Game Awards 2026 on December 10th, combined with a shadow drop, so mark your calendars.

The developer promises more details “soon,” but the teaser image provides a few hints. It features the silhouettes of Zoe, Auri and Saya, coincidentally the three most popular characters from a recent poll. Perhaps the update allows recruiting the latter two, who were introduced in 1.0 and the Sakurajima update as Tower Bosses.

That doesn’t quite answer why Zoe is standing side by side with them, however. But assuming they’re recruitable, can players also bring their respective Pals along as units? Time will certainly tell.

Of course, Pocketpair likely has even more planned with this major update, so stay tuned. All we know is that players shouldn’t expect No Man’s Sky -level support or simple additions like ten more levels to grind out.

Palworld is available for Xbox Series X/S, PS5, PC, and Xbox One. Check out our review of 1.0 here , which we praised for its addictive gameplay loop and new features (including the 72 new Pals).

items.title: v1.0.3: Balance Adjustments & Bug Fixes
items.summary: \ Palworld version v1.0.3 has been released! ＝＝＝ \ ▼Items and Equipment ・Changed the unlock level of some Jetragon-related technologies from 79 to 70, and reduced the materials required for the Pal Gear used to ride Jetragon. ・Changed the t
items.content:
\

Palworld version v1.0.3 has been released!

＝＝＝

\

▼Items and Equipment ・Changed the unlock level of some Jetragon-related technologies from 79 to 70, and reduced the materials required for the Pal Gear used to ride Jetragon.

・Changed the technology unlock level of the Aquatic Construction Kit from Level 66 to Level 23, changed its Ancient Technology Point requirement from 4 to 1, and adjusted the required materials and work amount.

・Extended the duration of World Tree Holy Water.

・Reduced the weight of World Tree Holy Water from 1 to 0.1.

・Added World Tree Holy Water to the rewards for World Tree expeditions, World Tree fishing, and the Large Fishing Pond.

・Increased the amount of World Tree Holy Water obtained from Pals in The World Tree area.

・Increased the amount of World Tree Holy Water obtained from Teafant Spring.

・Adjusted the work amount required to craft the Ancient Armor series.

・Doubled the amount of Fiber obtained from trees.

▼Bases and Missions

・Reduced the building costs of the Crude Oil Extractor, High-Pressure Crude Oil Extractor, and Large Power Generator.

・Increased the crude oil production speed of the Crude Oil Extractor and High-Pressure Crude Oil Extractor.

・The base mission that requires building a Crude Oil Extractor can now also be progressed by building a High-Pressure Crude Oil Extractor.

▼Server Settings

・Added a server setting (bAllowEnemyCampSpawnNearBaseCamp) that disables the suppression of enemy camp spawns near player base camps.

\

▼Graphics and Display

・Adjusted the boundary display in some areas to make it easier to see from a distance.

・Improved the display quality of some objects in dungeons.

▼Sound

・Added a sound effect when using World Tree Holy Water.

\

▼Crashes and Progression Blockers

・Fixed an issue where the mission could become impossible to progress if the barrier was removed before accepting the main mission in Sunreach.

▼Multiplayer and Co-op

・Fixed an issue in co-op where lighting on the client side could display incorrectly after cutscenes or the ending played.

・Fixed an issue in co-op where some scenes could stutter during the cutscene that plays when entering The World Tree.

・Fixed an issue on dedicated servers where Fast Travel could activate unintentionally during Tower Boss battles.

・Fixed an issue on dedicated servers where Pals could appear to vibrate rapidly on the client screen.

▼Pals and NPCs

・Fixed an issue where the summoned Pal could stop fighting.

・Fixed an issue where the summoned Pal could stop helping with base work.

・Fixed an issue in multiplayer where, when the Partner Skill of Orserk or certain other Pals activated, the effect display could fail to update correctly, making it appear as though the skill had not activated.

・Fixed an issue where Alpha Surfent would not produce Leather when assigned to a Ranch.

▼Battles and Bosses

・Fixed an issue where some raid boss battles could fail to progress as intended.

・Fixed an issue where the wave effect and actual damage range did not match for some of Panthalus's attacks.

▼Bases and Building

・Fixed an issue where the placement detection for stairs and slanted roofs could fail to match their actual shape.

・Fixed an issue where stairs could not be placed correctly on the sides of foundations or roofs.

▼Items and Rewards

・Fixed an issue where the reward settings for the normal Moon Lord battle and the Ultra Raid Boss battle had not been updated to the intended settings.

・Fixed an issue where items could duplicate when performing certain actions.

・Fixed an issue where, when Katress's Partner Skill activated, switching spheres while riding could allow the player to obtain a different type of sphere.

・Fixed an issue where the World Tree Holy Water effect did not display correctly on the Pal being ridden when using World Tree Holy Water while riding.

・Fixed an issue where, after the World Tree Holy Water effect ended, riding a Pal would cause the World Tree Holy Water aura to reappear and not disappear when approaching trees in The World Tree area.

・Fixed an issue where an unintended reward was set for the desert expedition.

・Fixed an issue where the Dark Skill Fruit: Psycho Gravity did not appear on the item search screen.

・Fixed a bug where the firing interval was not set for sphere launchers

▼UI, Display, and Text

・Fixed an issue where resolution settings would not apply correctly in fullscreen mode.

・Fixed an issue where, after switching window mode with F11 / Alt+Enter, the game could unintentionally return to fullscreen mode after loading.

・Fixed an issue where, if certain effects were on screen while aiming, the entire screen could become blurred.

▼Sound

・Fixed an issue where the water sound effect could fail to play at Teafant Spring.

・Fixed an issue on dedicated servers where the BGM for Attack Choppers triggered by other players could play even from far away.

・Adjusted the BGM playback range for Attack Choppers so that it plays correctly for players who are Wanted.

・Fixed an issue where unintended footstep sounds could play when walking on furniture or facilities.

▼Controls

・Fixed an issue where, after changing the key assignment for ""Attack that enemy!"" in Controls, selecting ""Restore to Default"" would not restore the default setting.

・Fixed an issue where settings could be applied unintentionally when interacting with the change confirmation dialog and duplicate key warning in Controls.

▼Map and Exploration

・Fixed an issue where a beach-like display could remain on the water surface after Fast Traveling to an offshore base.

＝＝＝

Thank you for your continued support of Palworld.

items.title: This New Survival Game Finally Clicked with Me, and I'm Never Looking Back
items.summary: Palworld 1.0 does a great job of easing you into its many complex systems.
items.content:
Survival games have been wildly popular for years now. I’ve dabbled here and there to see what the fuss is about, but I’ve always fallen off after a few hours. Usually, I get tangled up in one meagerly explained system after another until I lose track of what I’m supposed to do, and my time with the game peters out.

When Palworld 1.0 came out to rave reviews , I figured I’d give the genre another shot – and I’m glad I did. Palworld’s gradual, newbie-friendly onboarding helped me see what a whole lot of people have loved about survival games all along. Palworld made me a believer.

I’m glad I came in at the 1.0 mark, because I’ve heard Palworld had a much steeper learning curve out of the gate. But now, new players start with a series of missions designed to guide you through the game’s numerous systems . You learn how to punch trees to get wood to create a crafting bench. You learn how to make a club you can use to beat some Pals to death (it’s a dog-eat-dog world out there) to get wool. You then use that wool to make clothes. You set up a camp. You build a house. You activate a teleporter and explore deeper into the game world.

Before long, you’re gliding off cliffs Zelda-style before whomping on every Pal you see to catch them in spheres to put them to work. You can deploy them at your camp, ride them , or have them fight by your side to take on big roaming Pals and towering bosses . It’s a blast. And there’s no way I would have stuck with it if it hadn’t held my hand and eased me into the systems that make up the game.

I still have a long way to go, because I was nowhere near powerful enough to defeat the first boss solo. But those early missions gave me a much-needed handle on what else I can spend my time doing as I level up enough to become a threat. There's a vast world out there I can keep exploring, all while catching Pals and building up my base. I’m having a blast doing it.

Palworld’s 1.0 is available on Steam , Xbox , and PS5 . It costs $29.99, but you can save a few bucks on a Steam copy at Fanatical , which is currently running its summer sale .

Chris Reed is a commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. He also runs IGN's board game and LEGO coverage. You can follow him on Bluesky .

items.title: v1.0.2: Bug fixes
items.summary: \ Palworld version v1.0.2 has been released! This update includes improvements to gameplay stability and fixes for various issues. ＝＝＝ ▼Crashes and Disconnections ・Fixed an issue where all players could be disconnected during the Panthalus
items.content:
\

Palworld version v1.0.2 has been released!

This update includes improvements to gameplay stability and fixes for various issues.

＝＝＝

▼Crashes and Disconnections

・Fixed an issue where all players could be disconnected during the Panthalus battle on dedicated servers.

・Fixed an issue where players could crash during the Panthalus battle on dedicated servers.

・Fixed an issue where the game could crash when attempting Japanese text input in fullscreen mode.

▼Multiplayer

・Fixed an issue where, if a player was already in The World Tree area when the host transitioned to The World Tree area, the terrain could fail to display correctly from the host’s perspective.

・Fixed an issue where the Tower Boss “Victor & Shadowbeak” could disappear after using a teleportation attack during battle.

・Fixed an issue in the final boss battle where, if the host defeated the final boss while a guest was waiting to respawn, the guest’s light could fail to display correctly after respawning.

▼Missions

・Fixed an issue in the main mission “The First Islander” where the screen could remain faded out if dialogue was interrupted during a fade-out sequence.

・Fixed an issue in the sub-mission “Captured Adventurer” where the screen could remain faded out if dialogue was interrupted during a fade-out sequence.

▼Achievements

・Fixed an issue where the “Predator Hunter” achievement could fail to unlock even after meeting its requirements.

・Fixed an issue where the corresponding achievement could fail to unlock even after obtaining the required Pal Effigies.

・Fixed an issue on Xbox where the icons for two Lifmunk Effigy-related achievements were using outdated versions.

▼Graphics and Display

・Fixed an issue where the eye area of the player model could display incorrectly during cutscenes or certain player actions when using specific face types.

▼Controls

・Added key rebinding for "Attack that enemy!" and "Inventory".

・Fixed an issue where, when carrying over settings from versions earlier than v0.7, changes unrelated to Controls could still be treated as control setting conflicts.

・Fixed an issue where assigning a player action to the middle mouse button could incorrectly be treated as a conflict, preventing the setting from being applied.

・Fixed an issue where the Inventory Shortcut option was not displayed in Controls.

▼UI

・Fixed an issue where the damage number displayed when destroying ore while mining could sometimes appear as 0.

▼Performance Improvements

・Reduced the processing load during gameplay in Sunreach and improved performance.

＝＝＝

Thank you for your continued support of Palworld.
